plan:
This appears to be the "Pataka" hasta mudra - a classical Indian dance hand gesture. 

Key characteristics I observe from the target images:
- The hand is held upright/vertically with palm facing forward
- All four fingers (index, middle, ring, little) are extended and straight, held together closely or with minimal spread
- The thumb is extended outward to the side (abducted away from the fingers)
- The fingers are nearly parallel and vertical
- The palm faces the front camera
- The hand is in an open, dignified pose typical of classical Indian dance

Target finger positions:
- Index/middle/ring/little fingers: minimal flexion (mostly straight), brought together with slight or no abduction
- Thumb: abducted away from fingers (positive abd angle), extended (low flexion at mcp/ip joints)
- All finger joints should be relatively extended/straight to show the classical "flat hand" appearance
- The overall hand orientation shows the palm forward and fingers pointing upward

This appears to be the Shikara or Ikkshana mudra from Indian dance. The key features are:

1. Index and middle fingers are extended upward and spread apart
2. Ring and little fingers are curled/flexed down toward the palm
3. Thumb is bent and positioned, appearing to touch or come close to the ring/little fingers
4. The hand is oriented with palm facing forward and slightly to the side
5. The extended fingers (index and middle) are spread wide apart

Finger positioning:
- Index finger: extended (MCP ~0°, PIP ~0°, DIP ~0°), spread toward thumb side (abd ~15-20°)
- Middle finger: extended (MCP ~0°, PIP ~0°, DIP ~0°), spread away from index (abd ~-15-20°)
- Ring finger: flexed (MCP ~70-80°, PIP ~80-90°, DIP ~70°)
- Little finger: flexed (MCP ~70-80°, PIP ~80-90°, DIP ~70°)
- Thumb: flexed and opposed (cmc_flex ~40-50°, cmc_abd ~-20 to -30°, mcp ~30-40°, ip ~40-50°)

Hand orientation: Slight pitch forward, palm facing audience.
